findings.description: The KMS key used to encrypt the audit trail bucket does not set enable_key_rotation = true, so the key material is never automatically rotated. Long-lived key material increases the blast radius if the key is ever compromised and weakens cryptoperiod controls for audit log data.

No explicit key policy is defined, so the key falls back to the default policy that delegates full control to the account root, allowing any IAM principal in the account with kms:* permissions to use or administer the key that protects audit logs. An explicit least-privilege key policy should restrict decryption to the audit log consumers.
